In [[mathematics]], '''Jacobsthal sums''' are finite sums of [[Legendre symbol]]s related to [[Gauss sum]]s. They were introduced by {{harvs|txt|last=Jacobsthal|authorlink=Ernst Jacobsthal|year1=1907}}.

==Definition==

The Jacobsthal sum is given by
:<math>\phi_n(a)=\sum_{m\bmod p}\left(\dfrac{m(m^n+a)}{p}\right)</math>
where ''p'' is a prime and () is the [[Legendre symbol]].
